senses.en: a large building or group of buildings containing many different shops
examples: We meet at the **shopping centre** near the swimming pool.
The new **shopping centre** has a cinema on the top floor.
It rained, so we spent the afternoon in the **shopping centre**.

shopping centre.note: British English. Americans say **shopping mall** or just *the mall*. Note the British spelling *centre*.

senses.en: a large shop divided into sections, each selling a different type of goods
examples: She bought the shoes in a **department store**.
The **department store** has six floors.
Clothes are on the second floor of the **department store**.

department store.note: A **department store** is one shop with many sections; a *shopping centre* is many separate shops under one roof.

senses.en: a person who sells food or goods from a stall or cart in the street
examples: A **street vendor** was selling banh mi on the corner.
**Street vendors** line the road near the market.
We bought sugarcane juice from a **street vendor**.

forms.en: a person or company that sells something

senses.en: a table or small open shop in a market or at a fair, where things are sold
examples: Her family runs a fruit **stall** in the market.
There were twenty **stalls** at the school fair.
The **stall** opens at five in the morning.

senses.en: a person who buys goods or services from a shop or business
examples: The shop was full of **customers** on Saturday.
A good shop looks after its **customers**.
She is one of our regular **customers**.

customer.note: A **customer** buys goods; a *client* buys professional services; a *guest* stays at a hotel.

senses.en: something bought for much less than its usual price
senses.vi: món hời, món mua được giá rẻ
examples: These shoes were a real **bargain** at 200,000 dong.
The sale is full of **bargains**.
It's a **bargain** — buy it!

senses.en: to discuss a price with a seller in order to pay less
examples: You are expected to **bargain** at the market.
He **bargained** with the vendor for ten minutes.
She **bargained** the price down to half.

bargain.note: In British shops the price is fixed and you do not bargain; at a market you often can. *Haggle* means the same as the verb.

senses.en: an amount taken off the usual price
examples: Students get a 10% **discount**.
They offered me a **discount** because the box was damaged.
There is a **discount** on all winter coats.

discount.note: Stress the noun on the first syllable (**DIS**-count) and the verb on the second (dis-**COUNT**).

senses.en: money that is given back to you, especially because you have returned goods
examples: I took the shirt back and asked for a **refund**.
You can get a full **refund** within 14 days.
They gave me a **refund** without any trouble.

senses.en: to give someone their money back
examples: The shop **refunded** the full amount.
They will **refund** you if the item is faulty.

refund.note: Keep the **receipt** — most shops will not give a refund without one.

senses.en: a piece of paper showing that you have paid for something
examples: Keep the **receipt** in case you want a refund.
The cashier printed the **receipt**.
I lost the **receipt**, so I couldn't return it.

receipt.note: The **p** is silent: /rɪˈsiːt/, ri-**SEET**. A *receipt* proves you paid; a *bill* (BrE) or *check* (AmE) asks you to pay.

senses.en: money in the form of coins and notes rather than cards
examples: Do you want to pay by card or in **cash**?
Many street vendors only take **cash**.
I don't have enough **cash** on me.

cash.note: **Uncountable** — never *cashes*. Say *pay **in** cash* or *pay cash*, but *pay **by** card*.

senses.en: available in the shop and ready to be bought
examples: Do you have this jacket **in stock** in a smaller size?
The book is **in stock** at the city branch.
Sorry, we don't have that colour **in stock**.

senses.en: the act of taking goods to the person who has bought them
examples: **Delivery** is free on orders over 500,000 dong.
The **delivery** arrived two days late.
They offer next-day **delivery**.

forms.en: to take goods to a person or place

senses.en: to look at things in a shop without intending to buy anything in particular
examples: We spent an hour **browsing** in the bookshop.
I'm just **browsing**, thank you.
She likes to **browse** before she decides.

senses.en: to look through pages on the internet
examples: He was **browsing** the web on his phone.
I **browsed** a few online shops last night.

forms.en: a program used to look at internet pages
forms.ex: Open the link in a different **browser**.

browse.note: *I'm just browsing* is the polite English answer when a shop assistant asks if you need help.

senses.en: to put on a piece of clothing to see whether it fits and suits you
examples: Can I **try** these shoes **on**?
She **tried on** four dresses and bought none.
**Try** it **on** before you buy it.
colloc: a changing room to try things on

try on.note: Separable, and with a pronoun it **must** split: *try **it** on*, never *try on it*.

senses.en: a line of people waiting for something
examples: There was a long **queue** at the till.
Join the **queue** over there.
The **queue** moved surprisingly quickly.

senses.en: to wait in a line
examples: We **queued** for twenty minutes.
People were **queuing up** outside the shop.

queue.note: British English; Americans say *line* and *stand in line*. Pronounced simply /kjuː/ — like the letter **Q**; the last four letters are silent.

senses.en: useful and easy because it saves you time or trouble
examples: Online shopping is very **convenient**.
The shop is **convenient** for the bus station.
Would Saturday be **convenient** for you?

forms.en: the quality of being easy and useful

convenient.note: Opposite: **inconvenient**. Stress the second syllable: con-**VEN**-ient.

senses.en: costing a lot of money
examples: That jacket is too **expensive** for me.
Fruit is more **expensive** in winter.
It was the most **expensive** thing in the shop.

expensive.note: Opposite: **cheap** or *inexpensive*. Things are *expensive*; **prices** are *high*, not *expensive*.

senses.en: to buy something
examples: Tickets may be **purchased** online.
The company **purchased** new equipment.
Goods **purchased** in the sale cannot be returned.

senses.en: something you have bought, or the act of buying it
senses.vi: món hàng đã mua; việc mua
examples: Keep your receipt as proof of **purchase**.
She was pleased with her **purchases**.

purchase.note: **Formal.** In everyday speech use *buy*: you *buy* a coffee, but a company *purchases* equipment. Pronounced /ˈpɜːtʃəs/: **PUR**-chuss.

senses.en: a small label fixed to something in a shop, showing what it costs
senses.vi: nhãn ghi giá một mặt hàng
examples: Every item on the shelf has a **price tag**, so nobody bargains here.
Turn the mug over — the **price tag** is on the bottom.
She put the shirt back when she saw the **price tag**.

senses.en: the cost of something large, especially when the cost is surprising
examples: The new shopping centre came with a **price tag** of forty million dollars.
Free delivery sounds good, but it carries a hidden **price tag**.

price tag.note: Two words. A **price tag** is the label; the **price** is the number on it. Fixed price tags are what tell a supermarket from an open-air market, where goods carry none and buyers bargain.

senses.en: being sold for less than the usual price, for a short time
examples: These jeans are **on sale** this week: 400,000 dong instead of 600,000.
Winter coats go **on sale** in February.
I only bought it because it was **on sale**.

on sale.note: In British English **on sale** means *reduced*. To say that something can be bought at all, use **for sale**: *That house is **for sale***. American English blurs the two, so read the price before you celebrate.

senses.en: grown at home or in your own garden or fields, not bought from a supplier
examples: The tomatoes are **home-grown** — my grandfather grows them behind the house.
Most products at the fair were **home-grown** and cost very little.
She sells **home-grown** herbs at the farmers' market on Saturdays.

senses.en: coming from your own country or town rather than from abroad
senses.vi: cây nhà lá vườn, của địa phương
examples: The team is proud of its **home-grown** players.
The festival gives **home-grown** musicians a stage.

home-grown.note: Keep the hyphen. Use it for things that **grow**: vegetables, fruit, herbs, rice. Cakes and jam are not grown — they are **home-made**.

senses.en: made at home rather than bought from a shop or a factory
examples: My aunt bakes the cakes in her own kitchen, so they are **home-made**.
The stall sells **home-made** jam in old jam jars.
He took a jar of **home-made** chilli sauce back to school with him.

home-made.note: Keep the hyphen. **home-made** = made by hand at home; **home-grown** = grown at home. A **home-made** cake may be made from vegetables that are **home-grown**.

senses.en: someone who shops far more than they need to and finds it hard to stop
examples: She buys three pairs of shoes a month — she is a real **shopaholic**.
Online shops make it easy to become a **shopaholic**.
My cousin calls herself a **shopaholic**, but she never spends much.

forms.en: the habit of shopping too much
forms.ex: The talk was about **shopaholism** and how to spend less.

shopaholic.note: Informal, and built from *-aholic*, the ending of **alcoholic**. The same ending gives *workaholic* and *chocoholic*. A shopaholic is **addicted to** shopping.

senses.en: a small shop that sells food and everyday goods and stays open very long hours
examples: I need milk at eleven at night, so I go to the **convenience store** on the corner.
The **convenience store** near school is open 24/7.
A **convenience store** is quick, but its prices are higher than a supermarket's.

convenience store.note: You pay for the convenience: the shop is small, the range of products is narrow, and the prices are higher than in a supermarket. Note that the adjective **convenient** loses the *-ce*: *a convenient shop*, but *a convenience store*.

senses.en: a shop that sells only one or two particular kinds of goods
senses.vi: cửa hàng bán đồ chuyên dụng
examples: A florist's is a **speciality shop**: it sells flowers and very little else.
For running shoes she goes to a **speciality shop**, not a department store.
The old quarter is full of **speciality shops** — one street sells nothing but lanterns.

speciality shop.note: British **speciality** /ˌspeʃiˈæləti/ has five syllables; American English writes and says **specialty** /ˈspeʃəlti/ with three. The opposite kind of shop is a department store, which sells a wide range of products under one roof.

senses.en: a shop where everything costs the same low price, or close to it
examples: Everything in this shop is one dollar, so we call it a **dollar store**.
We bought the party plates and cups at a **dollar store**.
A **dollar store** is a cheap place to buy things you will only use once.

dollar store.note: Mainly American. British English says *pound shop*, and Vietnamese shops of this kind advertise as *cửa hàng đồng giá*. It is not the same as a **discount shop**, which sells ordinary goods at reduced prices rather than everything at one price.

senses.en: a market, usually held on the same day each week, where farmers sell what they have grown themselves
examples: The farmers sell their own vegetables at the **farmers' market** every Saturday.
My mother loves the **farmers' market** and rarely misses one.
Fruit at a **farmers' market** is picked the day before, not a week before.

farmers' market.note: The apostrophe comes **after** the *s*: the market belongs to the farmers, and there is more than one of them. Write *farmers' market*, not *farmer's market* or *farmers market*.

senses.en: the number of different kinds of goods a shop offers
examples: A big supermarket offers a wide **range of products**, from rice to raincoats.
The **range of products** in a convenience store is small.
Online shops can carry a huge **range of products** because they need no shelves.

range of products.note: **Wide**, not *big* or *large*: *a **wide** range of products*. The phrase is about **variety**, not quantity — a shop with a thousand identical umbrellas has a very narrow range.

senses.en: a notice, picture or short film that tries to make people buy something
examples: I saw an **advertisement** for that phone on my brother's tablet.
The coat is a different colour in the **advertisement**.
The newspaper carries three pages of **advertisements** for used bikes.

forms.en: to tell the public about something you want to sell
forms.ex: They **advertise** the sale on the shop window.
**Advertising** costs the company more than delivery does.

advertisement.note: British English stresses the second syllable: /ədˈvɜːtɪsmənt/, ad-**VER**-tis-ment. Short forms: **advert** (British) and **ad** (both, informal). Countable — *an advertisement*, *two advertisements*.

senses.en: something you say or write when you are not happy with something you have bought or been given
examples: I'd like to make a **complaint** about the shoes I ordered last week.
The shop has had three **complaints** about the same delivery driver.
Her **complaint** was polite: she described the problem and asked for a refund.

forms.en: to say that you are not happy with something
forms.ex: She **complained** about the price and got a discount.

complaint.note: **make** a complaint **about** something — never *for*. ❌ *a complaint for the shoes* ✅ *a complaint **about** the shoes*. With the verb: *complain **about** something* and *complain **to** somebody*.

senses.en: the chance or the right to use something, especially a service
senses.vi: khả năng, quyền truy cập hoặc tiếp cận
examples: Without Internet **access** you cannot shop online at all.
Every student has **access** to the reading room after four o'clock.
The village got **access** to clean water last year.

senses.en: a way of getting into a place
examples: **Access** to the car park is round the back of the centre.
The lift gives **access** to all four floors.

access.note: Uncountable: ❌ *an access* ✅ *access*. It takes **to**, not *of*: *access **to** the Internet*. Stress the first syllable, /ˈækses/ — **AC**-cess.

senses.en: unable to stop doing something, even when it is causing you trouble
examples: He is **addicted** to shopping — he cannot walk past a sale.
She says she is **addicted to** her phone and checks it every ten minutes.
A shopaholic is someone who is **addicted** to buying things.

forms.en: the state of not being able to stop
forms.ex: Online shopping can turn into an **addiction**.

addicted (to).note: Always **addicted to** + noun or **V-ing**: ✅ *addicted **to shopping*** ❌ *addicted to shop*. It goes after *be*, *become* or *get*, not in front of a noun.

senses.en: a list of the things you plan to buy
senses.vi: danh sách những thứ cần mua
examples: Write a **shopping list** before you go, or you will forget the rice again.
Rice, fish sauce and two lemons were the whole **shopping list**.
A **shopping list** is the cheapest way to stop yourself buying things you do not need.

shopping list.note: Two words. Things are **on** a shopping list, not *in* it: *Milk is **on** the list*. Used figuratively for any list of wants: *a shopping list of demands*.
